programs.title: Foodwise: Hangzhou Ep.2
programs.desc: In this episode, Tianran and Hannah continue their tea-tasting journey along Hangzhou's Qiantang River, exploring the region's historical culture and culinary delights. They head to Anding Mountain, enjoying misty tea at the summit. In Longmen Ancient Town, they dive into traditional Chinese clan culture and savor “Sun Quan seitan”. In the gentrified village of Shishe, Hannah falls in love with “gray soup rice dumplings”, while at Qiandao Lake Tianran tries the best fish head and beluga caviar he’s ever had in his life. Their journey ends with a cup of Jiukeng tea and a visit to ancient tea trees.

programs.title: Foodwise: Shantou
programs.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in Shantou, Guangdong Province in south China, where they drink more tea than anywhere else in the country. They'll savor the complex aroma of the curiously named \"Duck Poo Fragrance\" tea, as well as enjoy a more traditional \"yum cha\" breakfast. They get a taste of traditional handicrafts, from breaking bowls to make inlaid porcelain to rolling \"kueh\" rice cakes, and feast on everything from sweet and savory street snacks to the finest seafood dining.

programs.title: Foodwise: Shaoguan
programs.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in the picturesque city of Shaoguan in Guangdong Province, South China. They try tea grown on Danxia landforms and feast on mountain produce, before getting hands-on with making rice noodles in a Hakka walled village. They learn about the Hakka people’s southward migration and the effect it had on local tea and food, and end their journey in a thousand-year-old Buddhist temple, seeing how the monks integrate their practice into everyday life, and discovering just why tea is so important to Zen.

programs.title: China Highly Recommended: Changsha
programs.desc: Episode 1 of Travelogue's \"China Highly Recommended\" tells the story of Changsha, one of China's happiest cities. Following the lives of four of its foreign residents: A French executive chef, a Japanese podcaster, and two American teachers, we discover the reasons why they made Changsha their second home, and explore the city with them as only locals do. This episode will be released as a 30 minute travel documentary to be broadcast on CGTN's television channel and social media platform, along with a series of video clips and photos.

programs.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programs.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media – Changsha was China's first UNESCO \"Creative City\". It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. \nThe soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programs.title: Bird's-eye China Ep.4
programs.desc: Shaanxi, almost right in the middle of China, is a true land of contrasts. South of the Qinling Mountains that divide the province, the terrain has all the allure of south China, while north of this great dividing range lies the Guanzhong Plain and the austere and otherworldly Loess Plateau. Join us for a journey into a province that presents two equally beautiful and fascinating faces to the world.
